rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 <U+2014> two-year replicated field experiment (three 0.4 ha blocks) comparing SDI, DDI and furrow irrigation in organic processing tomato at Russell Ranch, with yield from machine harvests and water applied measured by flow meter. Q2: Section 3.1 and Fig. 1b <U+2014> SSD gave significant gains in IWP over furrow in both years with no significant yield decrease despite 17% (2015) and 36% (2016) less irrigation water applied. Q4: Section 3.2, Fig. 2 and Discussion <U+2014> soil gravimetric water content measured across the bed at three depths showed higher moisture in FI at 20-40 and 40-60 cm, interpreted as excess irrigation water in FI; discussion attributes short-term IWP gain to the reduced wetting volume of SSD. Q8: Discussion and Conclusions <U+2014> authors note the IWP gain is a short-term measure of crop per unit of water applied and overall system water use efficiency must account for soil structure and microbial shifts; study covers only the two years after SSD installation. Q9: Fig. 1 caption <U+2014> error bars indicate standard error for IWP.
rows.notes: IWP derived from one method (yield/applied water); single site, single crop, plot scale. Q4 is borderline: soil moisture distribution was measured rather than evaporation or drainage directly. No requirement-type support factors stated.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1 and 2.5 <U+2014> replicated field trial with weed counts in ten randomised quadrats per treatment per block in each of two years. Q2: Section 3.3 and Fig. 3 <U+2014> SSD treatments had fewer than 0.15 weeds m-2 in both years; weed density in FI was about 30 times (2015) and 100 times (2016) higher, with no difference between SDI and DDI.
rows.notes: Weed density measured by one method (quadrat counts) on a single date per year. Fig. 3 caption asserts the mechanism (reduced surface wetting prevents germination) but the measured 0-20 cm soil moisture did not differ significantly among treatments, so the intermediate variable is not shown; counted as assertion. Fig. 3 caption mentions only letter groupings, no standard error or other dispersion measure reported for weed counts. No weed-specific limitations or required conditions stated; single site, single crop, plot scale.
